Seminar Title:

Design of Metal Organic Framework (MOF) based Nanohybrid Photocatalysts for Activation of Atmospheric Molecules and Selective Organic Transformations

Seminar Type:

Synopsis Seminar

Department:

Chemistry

Speaker Name:

Saumyaranjan Panda ( Rollno : 521cy1014)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

Seminar Hall, Chemistry Department

Date and Time:

11 Nov 2026 11.00 AM

Contact:

Braja Gopal Mishra

Abstract:

Renewable H2 energy generation and green chemical manufacturing are two important focal points for the sustainable growth of modern civilization. The solar energy-assisted semiconductor photocatalysis technology can provide effective solutions to both these endeavours. In this research work, visible light harvesting high surface area metal organic framework (MOF) based nanohybrid materials have been designed and demonstrated as effective photocatalysts for green H2 reduction, O2 reduction and selective organic transformation reactions. Initially, the Cu-BDC-NH2 and MIL-88B(Fe) MOFs were prepared through facile solvothermal routes. The photo-redox features of the Fe-MOF are tuned by incorporating Ni2+ ions into the Fe3O clusters of the MOF lattice. The incorporation of Ni2+ ions and consequent generation of redox active ion pairs were investigated by using XPS, XAFS, TPD and ESR measurements. The as synthesized MOFs were subsequently in situ integrated with low band gap metal sulfides/mixed metal sulfides and complex oxide semiconductors to prepare the desired nanohybrid materials. Using this approach, four classes of nanohybrids, namely Cu-BDC-NH2/Cu58S32, Cs6W11O36/MIL-88B(Fe)-NH2, Cu2MoS4/MIL-88B(Fe,Ni) and Cu&shy58S32/MIL-88B(Fe,Ni)-NH2 were prepared. Comprehensive characterization of the nanohybrid materials revealed full spectrum absorption in UV Vis range, improved optoelectronic properties and higher charge carrier dynamics in comparison to the pure components. The photocatalytic efficacy of the Cu-BDC-NH2/Cu58S32 hybrid was studied for O2 reduction and H2 evolution reactions. The Fe-MOF-based nanohybrid materials were utilized for H2 production as well as selective oxidation reactions, including toluene oxidation to benzaldehyde, oxidative cleavage of C=C bond of cinnamaldehyde to benzaldehyde and anaerobic oxidation of benzyl alcohol to C-C coupling products. The detailed charge mobilization mechanisms in the nanohybrid materials and the reaction pathway for the organic transformations were elucidated using a combination of experimental and theoretical techniques. The important results generated and inferences drawn from these investigations will be presented in the seminar
